new.n: Lee Myre's Tavern, 2 miles north of Tomahawk on Hwy 51 (1936)
new.pl: Old US 51, about 2 miles north of Tomahawk, Lincoln County
new.st: A 1936 newspaper ad places Lee Myre's Tavern "2 Miles North on 51" from Tomahawk (Tomahawk Leader, 6 Aug 1936, p. 2). The pin is a placeholder 2 miles north of town; US 51 has since been rebuilt, so the old roadside lot still has to be found. There is no 1 m LiDAR for this stretch, and the 1938 air photo has not been read yet, so the pin is still only the 2-mile mark.
new.t: Roadhouse yards, parking areas and the ground by the door collect coins and tokens. Find the old 51 alignment on the 1938 aerial and look for a building lot 2 miles out. Private land: ask.
src: Tomahawk Leader, 6 Aug 1936, p. 2, ads (newspapers.com image 1238760030)
new.pinev: Placeholder 2 mi N of Tomahawk; Ground check to set on the 1930s Hwy 51 alignment

cd-road-lake-beach-tomahawk-1936.st: Road Lake also had a night club in 1936: the Road Lake Nite Club, run by Archie "Curley" Daigle, with dancing every night except Monday to the Road Lake Swingers (Tomahawk Leader, 6 Aug 1936, p. 2, ad). The club and the swimming spot together made Road Lake a summer crowd site.
src: Tomahawk Leader, 6 Aug 1936, p. 2, ads (newspapers.com image 1238760030)
